title: Scalar compatibility of the specified local cohomology-to-stalk class map
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism, $y\in Y$, $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $p\in\mathbb N$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $c:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$, $X′=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_Y X$, $f′:X′\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $g′:X′\to X$ the projections, and $F′=g′^*F$. Let $b:H^p(X′,F′)\to(c_*R^pf′_*F′)_y$ be the specified additive map [def-weil-pbc-local-direct-image-stalk-class-map], with $A$ acting on its source through Gamma-Spec followed by $f′.\mathrm{appTop}$. For every $r\in A$ and $x\in H^p(X′,F′)$, $b(r\cdot x)=r\cdot b(x)$. No invertibility assertion is made.

source.place: Lemma 20.7.3, the comparison of section-complex cohomology with higher direct-image sheaves; Tag 02OD, Lemma 30.20.7, the displayed local-stalk/global-cohomology equality, before formal functions. Scalar compatibility expanded by S4.

proof.text: Write A = O_{Y,y}, c = fromSpecStalk y, f′ the first projection, F′ the tensor pullback, and b the actual additive map of the cited definition. Represent r by a structure-sheaf section a on a neighborhood V. Mathlib Scheme.preimage_eq_top_of_closedPoint_mem and fromSpecStalk_closedPoint identify c inverse-image V with top. The germ/stalk-map identity Scheme.germ_stalkClosedPointTo, and stalkClosedPointTo_fromSpecStalk, identify c.app V a, transported to top, with Gamma-Spec.inv r. Hence the source r action is multiplication by f′.appTop (Gamma-Spec.inv r) on the section complex.

Expand b into its specified resolutionSectionClass, the higher-direct-image resolution isomorphism and the germ. The first resolution comparison is a morphism of modules over global functions of X′. For a fixed base section t, multiplication by its pullback is a chain endomorphism, because every differential is linear. Apply the naturality in the complex of the exact-functor cohomology comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to this endomorphism, both for forgetting module scalars and for evaluating presheaf modules on top. It identifies the induced homology map with multiplication by t. The identity of section complexes intertwines these multiplication endomorphisms. Evaluation of the presheaf cohomology and theta are linear over global functions of Spec A: theta is a presheaf-of-modules morphism. The higher-direct-image resolution comparison is a module-sheaf morphism and therefore linear on top sections. Thus the section before the final germ for r x is Gamma-Spec.inv r times the section for x.

Restrict the top section to V. Since c inverse-image V is top, this restriction is identity after the canonical identification, and the action of a is the same normalized global scalar found in step 1. PresheafOfModules.germ_smul now sends a times the section to r times its germ. Compose these identities to get b(r x) = r b(x). No injectivity or surjectivity is used: this proves only scalar compatibility. Zero modules, p = 0, and empty local base change satisfy the same calculation.

lean.statement:
theorem localDirectImage_stalk_class_smul {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (y : Y)
    (F : X.Modules) (p : ℕ) (r : Y.presheaf.stalk y)
    (x : (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology (pullback (Y.fromSpecStalk y) f).toRingedSpace p ⋙
      ModuleCat.restrictScalars
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of (Y.presheaf.stalk y))).inv ≫
          (pullback.fst (Y.fromSpecStalk y) f).appTop).hom).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.snd (Y.fromSpecStalk y) f)).obj F)) :
    localDirectImage_stalk_class f y F p (r • x) =
      r • localDirectImage_stalk_class f y F p x
